text: Applied to a linearly independent list v₁,…,vₙ, the Gram–Schmidt process produces:
choices: an orthonormal list e₁,…,eₙ with span(e₁,…,eₖ) = span(v₁,…,vₖ) for every k
a list of eigenvectors of the Gram matrix
an orthogonal list that may contain zero vectors
an orthonormal basis of the orthogonal complement of the span
explanation: At each step Gram–Schmidt subtracts the projections onto the previous vectors and normalizes, preserving all partial spans. Zero vectors would appear only if the input list were dependent; matrix-wise this is exactly the QR decomposition.
